EPIC: Service Workers Implementation
description:
Implement the W3C Service Workers specification with HTML dependencies mocked.

## Overview

Service Workers provide a programmable network proxy that runs independently of web pages, enabling offline support, push notifications, and background sync. This implementation will mock HTML dependencies (WorkerGlobalScope, event loop, script evaluation) and implement them fully later.

## Specification

- W3C Service Workers: https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/
- Local spec: specs/w3c/service-workers.md
- Local IDL: specs/idl/service-workers.idl

## Architecture

Service Workers consist of:
1. **Client-side APIs** (Window/Worker context): ServiceWorkerContainer, ServiceWorkerRegistration, ServiceWorker
2. **Global Scope** (SW context): ServiceWorkerGlobalScope, Clients, Client, WindowClient
3. **Events**: ExtendableEvent, FetchEvent, InstallEvent, ExtendableMessageEvent
4. **Cache API**: Cache, CacheStorage
5. **Core Algorithms**: Registration, Update, Install, Activate, Handle Fetch

## Dependencies

**Already Implemented:**
- URL (src/url/) - URL parsing, origins
- Fetch (src/fetch/) - Request/Response, fetch algorithm
- DOM Events (src/dom/) - EventTarget, Event dispatching
- Streams (src/streams/) - ReadableStream for body handling
- WebIDL (src/webidl/) - Type system
- Infra (src/infra/) - Lists, maps, sets
- Storage (src/storage/) - Storage keys, persistence

**To Be Mocked (from HTML):**
- WorkerGlobalScope base class
- Event loop for workers
- Script evaluation in worker context
- postMessage/MessagePort

## Implementation Strategy

1. Create HTML mocks for worker infrastructure
2. Implement core data structures and state machines
3. Implement client-side APIs (ServiceWorkerContainer, etc.)
4. Implement ServiceWorkerGlobalScope and related APIs
5. Implement events (ExtendableEvent, FetchEvent, etc.)
6. Implement Cache API
7. Implement core algorithms (registration, lifecycle, fetch handling)
8. Wire into existing Fetch implementation
9. Comprehensive testing

## Success Criteria

- All WebIDL interfaces implemented
- Service worker lifecycle (install, activate, update) working
- FetchEvent interception functional
- Cache API operational
- Navigation preload supported
- Comprehensive test coverage
- Zero memory leaks

title: Implement synchronous external script loading during parsing
description:
## Summary

Fetch and execute external scripts \(with src attribute\) synchronously during HTML parsing, blocking further parsing until the script completes.

## HTML Spec Reference

HTML Standard §4.12.1.1 "prepare the script element":
- Step 33: If script has src attribute \(external script\)
- Fetch the classic script resource
- For parser-inserted scripts without async/defer: parser-blocking
- Parsing pauses until fetch + execution completes

## Current State

`script_execution.zig` has `fetchExternalScript\(\)` which is already synchronous:
```zig
fn fetchExternalScript\(allocator: std.mem.Allocator, url: []const u8\) \!ExternalScriptFetchResult {
    // Uses std.http.Client for sync fetch
}
```

## Implementation

1. **Detect external scripts** in script execution callback:
   ```zig
   if \(HTMLScriptElementImpl.hasSrcAttribute\(script_element\)\) {
       const url = HTMLScriptElementImpl.getSrcAttribute\(script_element\)\;
       // Resolve URL against document base
       const resolved = resolveUrl\(url, document.baseURI\)\;
       // Fetch synchronously
       const result = try fetchExternalScript\(allocator, resolved\)\;
       // Set script text for execution
   }
   ```

2. **Parser-blocking behavior**:
   - Parsing is already paused in script callback
   - After fetch completes, execute script
   - Resume parsing after execution

3. **URL resolution**:
   - Resolve relative URLs against document base URL
   - Handle file:// URLs for WPT tests \(local files\)
   - Handle http:// URLs \(limited for WPT\)

4. **Error handling**:
   - Network error → fire error event, don't execute
   - Parse error → fire error event, don't execute
   - Set script result to null on error

## Files to Modify

- `src/html/script_execution.zig` \(already has most logic\)
- `src/html/script_execution_bridge.zig` \(wire up\)

## Test Criteria

```html
\<script src="external.js"\>\</script\>
\<script\>
  // This should see effects of external.js
  console.log\(window.fromExternal\)\; // defined in external.js
\</script\>
```

title: Epic: Eliminate @ptrCast - Fix WebIDL Inheritance Architecture
description:
**Critical architectural bug:** @ptrCast from child to parent types (Element→Node) reads garbage data due to incompatible struct layouts.

**Root Cause:** WebIDL codegen flattens parent fields and assumes field order = memory layout, but Zig reorders fields for optimization.

**Impact:** ~200 DOM tests fail with HierarchyRequestError

**Evidence:**
```zig
child.node_type = 1              // ✅ Direct access works
const node: *Node = @ptrCast(&child);
node.node_type = 51064           // ❌ Reads garbage!
```

**Solution:** Replace field flattening with composition pattern - eliminate @ptrCast entirely.

**Reports:** All analysis in `tmp/` directory:
- tmp/CODEGEN_REVIEW_SUMMARY.md
- tmp/PTRCAST_DEEP_REVIEW.md
- tmp/test_suite_analysis.md

**Effort:** 5-6 days
**Risk:** Medium (requires codegen refactor)
**Priority:** CRITICAL - Blocks all DOM testing

title: V8 FFI Segfault: Misaligned Address and Use-After-Free in WPT Runner
description:
## Summary

The WPT test runner crashes with a segfault around test 34 of 6346 tests due to multiple interrelated issues in the V8/Zig FFI boundary.

### Crash Signature


### Root Cause Analysis

Three parallel analyses identified the following root causes:

#### 1. Type Mismatch at FFI Boundary (CRITICAL)
- Zig FFI declares 
- C++ expects  (heap-allocated handle wrapper)
- Passing raw  instead of  causes V8 to dereference at wrong offset

#### 2. Use-After-Free via  Pattern (CRITICAL)
Multiple locations in  use:

The  schedules disposal BEFORE the return value is used by V8.

#### 3. Raw Timer Callback Pointers Without GC Protection (CRITICAL)
 stores raw V8 function pointers without persistent handles:

When GC collects the callback function between timer creation and firing → SEGFAULT

#### 4. Thread-Local State Not Reset Between Tests
-  hashmap accumulates across tests
- Stale timer callbacks can fire with invalid pointers
- Thread-local state may mismatch if V8 uses different thread

#### 5. Global Aliases Overwritten by testharness.js
-  errors indicate global setup issues
-  may be overwritten on harness reload

### Affected Files
-  - FFI declarations
-  - C++ wrapper
-  - Callback handling
-  - Interface bindings
-  - Test context management
-  - Browser adapter

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] WPT tests run without segfault through all 6346 tests
- [ ] No memory leaks detected
- [ ]  and  globals properly defined
- [ ] Timers work correctly across test boundaries
- [ ] No use-after-free detected by sanitizers

comments.author: bcardarella
comments.text:
Fixed DOMString ownership bug in EventTarget.addEventListener \(commit dcd926948\).

Root cause: The incoming DOMString from V8 was allocated with the V8 conversion layer's allocator, but EventTarget.deinit\(\) tried to free it with page_allocator, causing double-free or use-after-free.

Fix: Duplicate the DOMString with the internal allocator when storing in EventListenerRecord.

Remaining crashes found:
1. "Internal field out of bounds" in V8 Object - likely a separate issue with DOM node construction
2. Crashes in streams tests during Script execution - deeper V8 issue
3. Memory leaks in CharacterData.set_data - separate issue

comments.author: bcardarella
comments.text:
Additional fixes committed:

1. **Comment.zig** \(commit dd6ed71af\) - Fixed inheritance chain to properly chain CharacterData → Node → EventTarget
2. **DocumentType.zig** \(commit dd6ed71af\) - Fixed inheritance chain to properly chain Node → EventTarget  
3. **Node.cloneSingleNode** \(commit dd6ed71af\) - Register copy in node_internal_registry
4. **HTMLScriptElement.zig** \(commit 8b676fc42\) - Fixed inheritance chain to properly chain HTMLElement → Element → Node → EventTarget

These fixes eliminated the "Failed to append child in DOM: InvalidStateError" that was occurring during HTML parsing.

Remaining issues:
1. V8 "Internal field out of bounds" - happens after DOM tests progress further
2. Memory leaks in CharacterData.set_data - separate issue

The DOM tests now run much further before hitting V8 crashes.

# Epic: WebGPU Implementation (Future)

## Overview
Implement the WebGPU specification for GPU compute and graphics.

## Why This is a Separate Epic
WebGPU is a massive specification (~500 pages) that includes:
- 50+ WebIDL interfaces
- WGSL shader language
- Complex GPU pipeline management
- Requires native GPU backend (wgpu-native, Dawn)

This is effectively a project as large as the entire HTML implementation.

## Scope

- GPU, GPUAdapter, GPUDevice
- GPUBuffer, GPUTexture, GPUSampler

- GPUCommandEncoder, GPURenderPassEncoder, GPUComputePassEncoder

- GPURenderBundle, GPURenderBundleEncoder
- GPUQuerySet
- GPUCanvasContext
- ~40 more interfaces

### Backend Options
1. **wgpu-native** (Rust) - Mozilla/gfx-rs project
2. **Dawn** (C++) - Google's WebGPU implementation
3. **Custom** - Direct Vulkan/Metal/D3D12 abstraction

### Recommended Approach
Use wgpu-native via C FFI:
- Well-tested, cross-platform
- Supports Vulkan, Metal, D3D12, OpenGL
- Active development

## Current State
- navigator.gpu exists as NotImplemented stub

description:
## Overview

Implement the XMLHttpRequest state machine and open() algorithm following the WHATWG XHR specification. This is the foundation for all XHR request operations.

## Objectives

1. Implement XHR state machine with 5 states
2. Implement state transition logic with event firing
3. Implement open() algorithm with full validation
4. Create internal request/response state structures
5. Comprehensive unit tests for state transitions

## Spec References

- XHR Standard (states): https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#states
- XHR Standard (open): https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#the-open()-method  
- Fetch Standard (request): https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#requests

## Detailed Tasks

### Task 1: State Machine Implementation

**File:** src/xhr/internal/state_machine.zig

Create the complete state machine structure with all internal state per spec.

**Implementation:**
- 5 ready states (UNSENT, OPENED, HEADERS_RECEIVED, LOADING, DONE)
- All internal flags (send flag, timeout flag, etc.)
- Request state (method, URL, headers, body)
- Response state (response object, received bytes)
- State transition with automatic event firing

**Code skeleton provided in design doc**

### Task 2: open() Algorithm

**File:** src/xhr/algorithms/open.zig

Implement the complete open() algorithm with all validation steps.

**Steps:**
1. Validate and normalize HTTP method
2. Parse URL with base URL
3. Validate URL scheme
4. Handle username/password
5. Validate async mode
6. Terminate ongoing fetch

title: Fix 3 remaining WebIDL codegen compilation errors
description:
Fix 3 compilation errors in WebIDL generated code.

**Status**: 2/3 FIXED, 1 requires AST-based solution

**Errors**:

1. **AbstractRange.zig:152** - Unused allocator parameter ✅ FIXED
   - Fix: Added check for allocator usage, add '_ = allocator;' when not used
   - Location: src/webidl/codegen/codegen.zig line 3633+
   
2. **Attr.zig:209** - Pointless discard of used variable ✅ FIXED
   - Fix: Removed incorrect '_ = attribute;' discard from source
   - Location: webidl/src/dom/Attr.zig line 160

3. **Element.zig:1242** - Duplicate ShadowRoot import ⚠️ REQUIRES AST SOLUTION
   - Root cause: String-based method copying can't handle scope conflicts
   - Attempted fixes: String parsing insufficient (see analysis below)
   - Recommended solution: AST/IR-based codegen (6-7 hours)
   
**Analysis**:

The duplicate import issue reveals fundamental limitations of string-based code generation:

- **Problem**: Parent method has 'const ShadowRoot = @import...' locally, child has it at module level → shadowing error
- **Tried**: String parsing to remove local declarations
- **Failed**: Can't distinguish type imports (should remove) from module imports (must keep)
- **Result**: Removing all local imports breaks code; keeping them causes shadowing

**Why String Parsing Fails**:
1. Context-insensitive (can't distinguish import types)
2. Scope-unaware (can't track module vs local)
3. Incomplete (misses edge cases)
4. Cascading complexity (each fix needs more string manipulation)

**Recommended Solution: AST-Based Codegen**

Parse → IR → Optimize → Generate

Benefits:
- Proper scope tracking
- Clean optimization passes
- Maintainable code
- Future enhancements (dead code elimination, etc.)

**Detailed analysis**: tmp/codegen_ast_recommendation.md

**Decision Point**:
1. **Quick workaround**: Manually add ShadowRoot to all Node children (30 min, technical debt)
2. **Proper solution**: Implement AST-based codegen (6-7 hours, future-proof)

**Files Modified**:
- src/webidl/codegen/codegen.zig (allocator fix)
- webidl/src/dom/Attr.zig (removed discard, added ShadowRoot import)
- webidl/src/dom/Node.zig (added module-level ShadowRoot, removed local declarations)

**Recommendation**: Implement AST solution. String-based approach has reached its limits.

title: Update WPT runner to use parsed DOM for test execution
description:
## Summary

Modify the WPT runner to use the new HTML parsing infrastructure instead of manually extracting and executing scripts.

## Current Flow

1. Read .html file
2. Create empty Document
3. Extract `\<script\>` tags manually \(test_parser.zig\)
4. Execute scripts in empty document

## Target Flow

1. Read .html file content
2. Parse HTML using HTMLParser.parseHTML\(\) with scripting enabled
3. Scripts execute automatically during parsing via callbacks
4. DOMContentLoaded fires
5. Run event loop for async tests
6. Collect results

## Implementation

1. **Modify BrowserAdapter.runTest\(\)**:
   ```zig
   pub fn runTest\(self, test_path: []const u8, test_content: []const u8, timeout: Timeout\) \!TestResult {
       var ctx = try BrowserContext.init\(self.allocator, .window, self.wpt_root\)\;
       defer ctx.deinit\(\)\;
       
       try ctx.initialize\(\)\;
       try ctx.loadTestHarness\(\)\;
       
       // NEW: Parse HTML instead of extracting scripts
       try ctx.parseAndExecuteHTML\(test_content\)\;
       
       // Run event loop for async tests
       try ctx.runEventLoop\(timeout.toMillis\(\)\)\;
       
       return ctx.result_collector.finalize\(self.allocator, test_path\)\;
   }
   ```

2. **Add parseAndExecuteHTML to BrowserContext**:
   - Creates HTMLParser with script callback wired to V8
   - Parses the HTML content
   - Scripts execute during parsing
   - Fires DOMContentLoaded

3. **Remove manual script extraction**:
   - test_parser.zig script extraction no longer needed
   - Scripts run at correct time during parsing

4. **Handle .js vs .html tests**:
   - .html tests: Use full HTML parsing
   - .js tests: Continue with current approach \(wrap in minimal HTML\)

- `tests/wpt_runner/browser_adapter.zig`

### constructorCallback \(Line ~1473-1579\)
Entry point for all WebIDL interface constructors. Extracts arguments from V8 and calls the Zig constructor.

```zig
pub fn getInstance\(comptime T: type, object: *v8.Object\) ?*T {
    const ptr = v8.v8_Object_GetAlignedPointerFromInternalField\(object, 0\)\;
    if \(ptr == null\) return null\;

}
```
This receives a V8 Object - verify the object pointer itself isn't tagged.

title: Phase 3, Week 5: Synchronous send() with Event Loop
description:
## Overview

Implement synchronous XMLHttpRequest using the existing event loop to spin until the response completes. This matches browser behavior (Chromium/Firefox/WebKit) by running the event loop in a blocking manner while allowing network I/O to progress.

## Objectives

1. Implement synchronous send() path
2. Integrate with event loop (tick until complete)
3. Implement synchronous error handling (throw exceptions)
4. Validate synchronous restrictions (forbidden in Workers)
5. Comprehensive tests for sync mode

## Spec References

- XHR Standard (send sync): https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#the-send()-method step 12
- HTML Standard (pause): https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#pause

## Browser Implementation

All browsers use nested event loop / "pause" semantics:
- Network I/O remains async underneath
- JavaScript execution blocks
- Event loop continues processing network events only
- No progress events fire during sync request
- Errors throw exceptions instead of firing events

## Implementation Strategy

Use existing event loop (`src/runtime/event_loop/`) with `tick()` to spin until response complete.

## Detailed Tasks

See implementation plan for complete sendSync() algorithm using event_loop.tick()

## Acceptance Criteria

- Synchronous send() blocks until complete
- Event loop spins correctly
- No progress events during sync
- Errors throw exceptions (not events)
- Timeout throws TimeoutError
- Forbidden in Workers (validation)
- Tests pass

## Estimated Effort

1 week

1. **WptServer** ✅ - Start/stop wpt serve process

Handle circular import prevention for dictionaries
description:
Dictionaries can reference types that reference dictionaries back, creating potential circular imports.

Example cycle: RequestInit -> HeadersInit (typedef) -> Headers (interface) -> RequestInit (constructor arg)

Strategy to prevent cycles:

1. For typedef imports in dictionaries: Use forward declaration pattern
   - typedefs.zig already handles this by using anyopaque for circular refs

2. For dictionary-to-dictionary references:
   - Import specific dictionary file, not root
   - Example: @import("OtherDict.zig") instead of @import("dictionaries")

3. For interface references in dictionaries:
   - Use runtime.Instance pointer (already works)
   - Interfaces import dictionaries, not vice versa

4. Add cycle detection in type resolution:
   - Track which types are currently being processed
   - If a type is encountered while processing itself, use opaque pointer

Testing: Find or create test case with circular dictionary references.

description:
Implement the constructor string parser for shorthand URL patterns.

## Location
`src/urlpattern/constructor_string_parser.zig`

## Purpose

Parses shorthand pattern strings like:
- `"https://example.com/:path"`
- `"*://*/*.js"`
- `"/api/:version/users/:id"`

Into URLPatternInit with individual component patterns.

## Algorithm: parse a constructor string

Per spec, this is a state machine that:
1. Identifies protocol, hostname, port, pathname, search, hash
2. Handles pattern syntax within each component
3. Returns URLPatternInit dictionary

## State Machine

```zig
const State = enum {
    init,
    protocol,
    authority,
    username,
    password,
    hostname,
    port,
    pathname,
    search,
    hash,
    done,
}\;

const ConstructorStringParser = struct {
    input: []const u8,
    state: State,
    index: usize,
    
    // Component accumulators
    protocol_value: []const u8,
    username_value: []const u8,
    password_value: []const u8,
    hostname_value: []const u8,
    port_value: []const u8,
    pathname_value: []const u8,
    search_value: []const u8,
    hash_value: []const u8,
    
    pub fn parse\(allocator: Allocator, input: []const u8\) \!URLPatternInit\;
}\;
```

## Key Transitions

- `://` after protocol → authority state
- `@` in authority → username:password separator
- `:` after hostname → port
- `/` after authority → pathname
- `?` → search
- `#` → hash

## Pattern-Aware Parsing

Must handle pattern syntax within each component:
- Groups `{...}` - don't treat as URL syntax
- Named params `:name` - preserve
- Regexp `\(...\)` - preserve \(but track depth\)
- Wildcards `*` - preserve

```zig
fn consumeToDelimiter\(self: *Parser, delimiters: []const u8\) []const u8 {
    var group_depth: usize = 0\;
    var regexp_depth: usize = 0\;
    
    while \(self.index \< self.input.len\) {
        const c = self.input[self.index]\;
        
        // Track pattern syntax depth
        if \(c == '{'\) group_depth += 1\;
        if \(c == '}' and group_depth \> 0\) group_depth -= 1\;
        if \(c == '\('\) regexp_depth += 1\;
        if \(c == '\)' and regexp_depth \> 0\) regexp_depth -= 1\;
        
        // Only check delimiters at depth 0
        if \(group_depth == 0 and regexp_depth == 0\) {
            if \(mem.indexOfScalar\(u8, delimiters, c\) \!= null\) break\;
        }
        
        self.index += 1\;
    }
    // return accumulated string
}
```

## Spec Reference
URLPattern spec "parse a constructor string" algorithm.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Full URLs parsed correctly
- [ ] Relative paths work
- [ ] Patterns within components preserved
- [ ] All component delimiters recognized
- [ ] Username:password syntax works
- [ ] IPv6 hostnames handled

description:
## Epic: WHATWG TestUtils Standard Implementation

### Specification
- **Spec URL**: https://testutils.spec.whatwg.org/
- **Scope**: TestUtils namespace with gc() method
- **Exposure**: Window, Worker contexts

### Summary
Implement the complete WHATWG TestUtils Standard, which provides in-browser APIs for testing browser implementations. The primary (and currently only) API is `TestUtils.gc()` which triggers garbage collection asynchronously and returns a Promise.

### Key Requirements
1. **Compile-time gating**: Only available with `-Denable-test-utils=true`
2. **Engine abstraction**: All calls through EngineInterface, no direct V8 coupling
3. **Dedicated GC thread**: True "in parallel" execution per spec
4. **Context type infrastructure**: Window/Worker distinction via new Realm module
5. **Full test coverage**: Unit, V8 integration, and JavaScript E2E tests

### Architecture Decisions
- GC runs on dedicated background thread (spec says "in parallel")
- Promise resolution scheduled back to main thread via new EngineInterface method
- Engine decides GC strategy (V8 uses Isolate-level full GC)
- Realm/ContextType infrastructure in new `src/runtime/realm.zig`
- Flat module structure: `src/testutils/{root,gc,context}.zig`

### Dependencies
- Depends on: None (foundational work)
- Blocks: Future TestUtils additions, web-platform-tests integration

### Success Criteria
- [ ] `TestUtils.gc()` returns Promise<undefined>
- [ ] GC executes on dedicated thread
- [ ] Promise resolves after GC completes
- [ ] Only available when build flag enabled
- [ ] Works in both Window and Worker contexts
- [ ] All tests pass (unit, integration, E2E)

title: Implement Promise wrapper for synchronous fetch result
description:
Wrap the synchronous fetch result in a V8 Promise for proper Web API semantics.

## Problem
- globalFetch() returns synchronous FetchResult
- Web fetch() API returns Promise<Response>
- V8 callbacks need to return Promises for promise_test() to work

## Solution Options

### Option A: Wrap at V8 Boundary
- Let Zig fetch remain synchronous
- Wrap result in resolved Promise in V8 layer
- Simplest approach if async not needed

### Option B: Async Fetch with Callback
- Make fetch truly async with callbacks
- Create Promise, resolve when fetch completes
- Better for future network operations

### Option C: Use V8 Promise Resolver
- Create V8 Promise with resolver
- Immediately resolve with result
- Clean integration with V8 Promise machinery

Blocker: ArrayBufferView Runtime API for BYOB Streams
description:
Implement ArrayBufferView runtime API to enable BYOB (Bring Your Own Buffer) stream operations.

## Problem

BYOB operations in ReadableByteStreamController and ReadableStreamBYOBReader require introspection and manipulation of ArrayBufferView objects, but the runtime API is incomplete.

## Affected Files

- src/webidl/impls/ReadableByteStreamController.zig (12+ TODOs)
- src/webidl/impls/ReadableStreamBYOBReader.zig (6+ TODOs)
- src/webidl/impls/ReadableStreamBYOBRequest.zig (2+ TODOs)
- src/runtime/arraybuffer_view.zig

## Required API Functions

1. **Buffer introspection**
   - getViewByteLength(view) - Get byte length of view
   - getViewByteOffset(view) - Get byte offset into buffer
   - getViewBuffer(view) - Get underlying ArrayBuffer
   - isViewDetached(view) - Check if buffer is detached

2. **View construction**
   - createView(ViewConstructor, buffer, byteOffset, length) - Create typed array view
   - ViewConstructor enum: Uint8Array, Int8Array, Uint16Array, etc.

3. **Buffer operations**
   - transferArrayBuffer(buffer) - Transfer ownership (detach source)
   - cloneArrayBuffer(buffer, offset, length) - Clone portion of buffer

## Implementation Approach

1. Define ArrayBufferView abstraction in runtime
2. Implement V8 FFI bindings for buffer operations
3. Add view construction for all TypedArray types
4. Implement buffer transfer/clone per spec

## Success Criteria

- [ ] All getView* functions implemented and tested
- [ ] View construction works for all TypedArray types
- [ ] Buffer transfer/clone work correctly
- [ ] ReadableByteStreamController.enqueue() works with real views
- [ ] ReadableStreamBYOBReader.read() works with user buffers

## Estimated Effort

3-5 days

## Dependencies

- V8 FFI infrastructure (complete)

## Spec References

- WHATWG Streams § 4.7 ReadableByteStreamController
- ECMAScript § 25.1 ArrayBuffer Objects
- ECMAScript § 23.2 TypedArray Objects

title: WS-01: Create src/websocket/ directory structure and module skeleton
description:
## Summary

Create the foundational directory structure and module skeleton for the WebSocket implementation.

## Directory Structure

```
src/websocket/
├── protocol/
│   ├── frame.zig           # Frame parsing and serialization
│   ├── masking.zig         # XOR masking operations
│   ├── handshake.zig       # Handshake key generation and validation
│   ├── opcodes.zig         # Opcode constants and utilities
│   ├── close_codes.zig     # Close status codes per RFC 6455 §7.4.1
│   └── root.zig            # Protocol module root
├── connection/
│   ├── state_machine.zig   # Connection state transitions
│   ├── buffer.zig          # Send/receive buffering
│   └── root.zig
├── network/
│   ├── transport.zig       # Abstract transport interface
│   ├── tcp_transport.zig   # Raw TCP implementation
│   ├── tls_transport.zig   # TLS wrapper for wss://
│   └── root.zig
├── events.zig              # Event creation and dispatching
├── websocket.zig           # Main WebSocket connection logic
└── root.zig                # Public API exports
```

## Tasks

1. Create all directories listed above
2. Create root.zig files that export submodules
3. Add to src/root.zig: `pub const websocket = @import("websocket/root.zig");`
4. Create placeholder structs/functions with `@compileError("TODO")` for unimplemented
5. Ensure `zig build` passes with the new structure
6. Add basic module documentation headers

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All directories and files created
- [ ] Module exports work (`@import("websocket").protocol.frame` etc.)
- [ ] `zig build` passes
- [ ] `zig build test` passes (even with empty tests)

## Dependencies

None - this is the foundation issue.

## Estimated Effort

1-2 hours

## Problem

In  lines 109-136, the  function nullifies template entries but never calls  to properly release the V8 Global handles.



V8 Global handles continue pointing to freed isolate memory after disposal, causing use-after-free when the next isolate is created and templates are accessed.

## Root Cause

V8 FunctionTemplates are stored as Global handles that must be explicitly disposed before the isolate is destroyed. Simply setting pointers to null leaks the Global handle and leaves V8 internal state corrupted.

## Solution

Add proper disposal before clearing each entry:

Browser-like HTML Parsing with Script Execution in WPT Runner
description:
## Overview

The WPT runner currently creates an empty Document object and manually extracts `\<script\>` tags from HTML files, running scripts in the empty document. This causes failures like `document.querySelector\("meta[charset]"\)` returning null because the HTML is never actually parsed into a DOM tree.

## Goal

Implement browser-like HTML parsing that:
1. Parses HTML into a real DOM tree using the full HTML parser
2. Executes scripts during parsing at the correct time \(when `\</script\>` is hit\)
3. Supports `document.write\(\)` during parsing
4. Handles external script loading
5. Fires DOMContentLoaded when parsing completes

## What We Have

**Full HTML Parser** \(`src/html/parser/`\):
- 80-state tokenizer \(`tokenizer.zig`\)
- 24-mode tree builder \(`tree_builder.zig`\)
- Fragment parsing \(`fragment_parser.zig`\)
- Script execution callback support \(`setScriptExecutionCallback`\)
- Document write support \(`document_write.zig`\)

**HTMLParser Integration** \(`src/webidl/impls/HTMLParser.zig`\):
- `parseHTML\(\)` - parses HTML string to DOM Document
- `parseFragment\(\)` - parses fragment to DocumentFragment
- `convertTreeNodeToDom\(\)` - converts TreeNode tree to DOM nodes

**Script Execution** \(`src/html/script_execution.zig`\):
- Script preparation algorithms
- Script execution algorithms

**WPT Runner** \(`tests/wpt_runner/`\):
- `browser_context.zig` - creates browser-like V8 context
- `browser_adapter.zig` - runs tests
- Currently creates empty Document, doesn't use HTML parser

## Key Challenges

1. **TreeNode ↔ DOM Node conversion during parsing**: The tree builder works with TreeNode, but script execution needs DOM nodes. Currently conversion happens after parsing is complete.

2. **Script execution callback integration**: Tree builder has `setScriptExecutionCallback` but nobody uses it. Need to wire this up to actual V8 script execution.

3. **document.write\(\) support**: Scripts can inject content into the parser input stream. The `document_write.zig` module exists but needs integration.

4. **External script loading**: Need to fetch external scripts, possibly async.

5. **Incremental DOM building**: Currently `convertTreeNodeToDom` runs after parsing. For script execution to work, DOM nodes need to exist when scripts run.

## Success Criteria

- `document.querySelector\("meta[charset]"\)` works in WPT tests
- Scripts execute during parsing at the correct time
- `document.write\(\)` works during parsing
- External scripts can be loaded and executed
- DOMContentLoaded fires appropriately

## Implementation Strategy

Phase 1: Foundation - Enable HTMLParser usage in WPT runner
Phase 2: Script Integration - Wire up script execution callback
Phase 3: document.write\(\) - Enable dynamic content insertion
Phase 4: External Scripts - Fetch and execute external scripts
Phase 5: Events - Fire DOMContentLoaded and related events

title: EPIC: Complete WHATWG Fetch Standard Implementation (100%)
description:
Implement all missing Fetch algorithms, integrate libcurl for real HTTP/HTTPS requests, add ReadableStream body streaming, wire cache/cookies, and create comprehensive test suite with mock HTTP server.

## Overview

Complete the WHATWG Fetch Standard implementation to 100% spec compliance. Currently ~60% complete with excellent data structures but missing critical network I/O.

## Current Status

**What Works**:
- ✅ Complete internal data structures (Request, Response, Headers)
- ✅ Spec-compliant algorithm flow (fetch → main fetch → HTTP fetch)
- ✅ Full data: URL support
- ✅ CORS check algorithm
- ✅ Cookie store (RFC 6265bis)
- ✅ Cache structures (RFC 9111)

**Critical Gaps**:
- ❌ LibcurlBackend - All HTTP(S) requests return fake 200 OK
- ❌ ReadableStream Body - Uses byte arrays, can't stream large files
- ❌ Network integration - Stub at http_fetch.zig:200-214
- ❌ WebIDL interface implementations wrong location (src/fetch/webidl/ instead of src/webidl/impls/)
- ⚠️ Cache not wired into fetch flow
- ⚠️ Cookies not sent/received
- ⚠️ AbortSignal not checked

## Architecture Problems to Fix

### CRITICAL: WebIDL Interface Architecture is WRONG

**Current (Broken)**:
```
src/webidl/
  interfaces/          ← Generated (correct)
  impls/              ← STUBS returning error.NotImplemented (WRONG!)
  
src/fetch/
  webidl/             ← DUPLICATE implementations in WRONG location! (12K+ lines)
    headers.zig
    request.zig
    response.zig
  internal/           ← Real data structures (correct location)
    request.zig
    response.zig
    header_list.zig
```

**Should Be**:
```
src/webidl/
  interfaces/          ← Generated WebIDL interfaces
  impls/              ← REAL implementations using src/fetch/internal/
    Headers.zig       ← Implement using internal.HeaderList
    Request.zig       ← Implement using internal.InternalRequest
    Response.zig      ← Implement using internal.InternalResponse
    
src/fetch/
  internal/           ← Internal data structures (keep as-is)
    request.zig
    response.zig
    header_list.zig
  algorithms/         ← Fetch algorithms (keep as-is)
  webidl/             ← DELETE THIS! Wrong architecture!
```

**Why This is Critical**:
- WebIDL impls should wrap internal Fetch structures, not duplicate them
- src/fetch/webidl/ is architectural mistake - duplicates interface layer
- Currently generated interfaces import stubs, not real code
- Need single source of truth: internal structures in src/fetch/internal/

## Success Criteria

- All HTTP(S) requests use libcurl (not stubs)
- Can fetch from real servers (google.com, github.com)
- Streaming works for large files (multi-GB)
- CORS preflight passes
- Cookies persist across requests
- AbortController cancels in-flight requests
- Cache reduces redundant requests
- All WebIDL interfaces properly implemented in src/webidl/impls/
- src/fetch/webidl/ removed (architectural cleanup)
- WebIDL impls use src/fetch/internal/ structures
- Mock HTTP server for integration tests
- 90%+ test coverage
- Zero memory leaks
- Full documentation

## Timeline

12 weeks across 9 phases (added Phase 0 for architecture refactor)

- tmp/fetch_spec_complete_inventory.md
- tmp/analysis/fetch_implementation_inventory.md

title: Document TransformStream internal vs JavaScript construction patterns
description:
## Summary

Document the correct patterns for calling TransformStream from Zig code \(internal construction\) vs from JavaScript \(via WebIDL bindings\).

## Documentation Location

Add to one of:
- `tmp/analysis/TRANSFORM_STREAM_PATTERNS.md` \(temporary analysis\)
- OR add inline documentation to `src/webidl/impls/TransformStream.zig`

## Content to Document

### 1. JavaScript Construction \(via WebIDL\)

When JavaScript creates a TransformStream:
```javascript
new TransformStream\({
    transform\(chunk, controller\) { ... },
    flush\(controller\) { ... }
}\)\;
```

The `transformer` parameter is a V8 Object containing JavaScript callback functions. The WebIDL binding converts this to `*const anyopaque` which is actually a tagged V8 Global handle.

### 2. Internal Zig Construction

When Zig code creates a TransformStream \(e.g., TextDecoderStream, TextEncoderStream\):
- The transformer parameter should be `notPassed\(\)` 
- Internal algorithms should be set up via Zig code, not JavaScript callbacks
- DO NOT pass arbitrary Zig pointers as the transformer

### 3. Correct Pattern for Internal Streams

```zig
// CORRECT: No transformer, will use internal algorithms
const transform = try interfaces.TransformStream.call_constructor\(
    allocator,
    ctx,
    webidl.Opt\(*const anyopaque\).notPassed\(\),  // No JS transformer
    webidl.Opt\(dictionaries.QueuingStrategy\).notPassed\(\),
    webidl.Opt\(dictionaries.QueuingStrategy\).notPassed\(\),
\)\;

// Set up internal transform/flush algorithms via the controller
const controller = transform.getController\(\)\;
controller.setTransformAlgorithm\(myZigTransformFn\)\;
controller.setFlushAlgorithm\(myZigFlushFn\)\;
```

### 4. Anti-Pattern \(What NOT to do\)

```zig
// WRONG: Passing a Zig stack pointer as transformer
var placeholder: u8 = 0\;
const transform = try interfaces.TransformStream.call_constructor\(
    allocator,
    ctx,
    webidl.Opt\(*const anyopaque\).passed\(\&placeholder\),  // BUG\!
    ...
\)\;
```

### 5. Why This Matters

The `*const anyopaque` type is used because:
1. JavaScript transformers are V8 Objects \(tagged Global handles\)
2. WebIDL needs a type that can represent "any JavaScript value"
3. But Zig code should NOT abuse this to pass arbitrary Zig pointers

The TransformStream code assumes the pointer IS a V8 Object and will crash if given a Zig pointer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Documentation created explaining both patterns
- [ ] Anti-pattern clearly documented with explanation
- [ ] Code examples provided for correct usage
- [ ] Added to appropriate location \(inline docs or analysis file\)

description:
## Summary

Implement async script loading: scripts with async attribute fetch in parallel and execute as soon as they're ready, potentially out of order.

## HTML Spec Reference

HTML Standard §4.12.1.1:
- Step 35.3-35.4: If async and src
- Add to "set of scripts that will execute as soon as possible"
- Execute when ready \(fetch complete\), regardless of document order
- force_async flag: scripts added without async but dynamically become async

## Current State

`script_execution.zig` has:
- `addScriptToExecuteAsap\(\)` - adds to async set
- `executeScriptsAsap\(\)` - executes ready scripts

## Implementation

1. **Async script set on Document**:
   ```zig
   scripts_to_execute_asap: std.AutoHashMap\(*runtime.Instance, void\),
   ```

2. **Start async fetch**:
   - When script element prepared with async
   - Start fetch without blocking parser
   - Continue parsing immediately

3. **Execute when ready**:
   - Poll pending scripts
   - When fetch completes, mark ready
   - Execute ready scripts \(any order\)

4. **Integration with event loop**:
   - In WPT runner event loop, check for ready async scripts
   - Execute between microtask checkpoints

5. **force_async flag**:
   - Scripts added dynamically get force_async = true
   - Unless they have async attribute set

## Async vs Parser-Blocking

```
Parser-blocking:  Parse → Fetch → Execute → Parse
Async:           Parse ─────────────────→ Parse
                       ↘ Fetch → Execute ↗
```

## Files to Modify

- `src/webidl/impls/Document.zig` \(add async set\)
- `src/html/script_execution.zig` \(async logic\)
- `tests/wpt_runner/browser_context.zig` \(event loop integration\)

## Test Criteria

```html
\<script\>window.order = []\;\</script\>
\<script async src="slow.js"\>\</script\>   \<\!-- takes 100ms --\>
\<script async src="fast.js"\>\</script\>   \<\!-- takes 10ms --\>
\<\!-- fast.js should execute before slow.js --\>
```

title: Phase 5: DOM Range Operations (13 algorithms)
description:
Implement Range interface algorithms for text selection and editing.

**Estimated Effort**: 2-3 weeks
**Priority**: P2 (MEDIUM)
**Requires**: Phase 1 complete (cloneNode needed for cloneContents)

**Spec Reference**: specs/dom.md §6 (Interface Range)

**Algorithms to Implement**:

**Boundary Manipulation (6 methods)**:

1. **Range.setStart(node, offset)** - Set start boundary
   - Spec: specs/dom.md lines ~5000-5050
   - Complexity: MEDIUM (boundary validation, position comparison)
   - Test: Valid positions, invalid nodes, offset out of bounds

2. **Range.setEnd(node, offset)** - Set end boundary
   - Spec: specs/dom.md lines ~5050-5100
   - Complexity: MEDIUM (boundary validation, position comparison)
   - Test: Valid positions, end before start correction

3. **Range.setStartBefore(node)** / **setStartAfter(node)**
   - Spec: specs/dom.md lines ~5100-5150
   - Complexity: LOW (uses setStart internally)
   - Test: Valid nodes, root node, detached nodes

4. **Range.setEndBefore(node)** / **setEndAfter(node)**
   - Spec: specs/dom.md lines ~5150-5200
   - Complexity: LOW (uses setEnd internally)
   - Test: Valid nodes, root node, detached nodes

5. **Range.collapse(toStart?)** - Collapse range to single position
   - Spec: specs/dom.md ~line 5250
   - Complexity: LOW (copy start to end or vice versa)
   - Test: Collapse to start, collapse to end

6. **Range.selectNode(node)** / **selectNodeContents(node)**
   - Spec: specs/dom.md lines 5260-5300
   - Complexity: LOW (set boundaries around/inside node)
   - Test: Element nodes, text nodes, document nodes

**Comparison (2 methods)**:

7. **Range.compareBoundaryPoints(how, sourceRange)** - Compare boundaries
   - Spec: specs/dom.md lines 5320-5380
   - Complexity: MEDIUM (position comparison with 4 modes)
   - Test: All 4 comparison modes, same/different ranges

8. **Range.isPointInRange(node, offset)** / **comparePoint(node, offset)**
   - Spec: specs/dom.md lines 5880-5920
   - Complexity: LOW
   - Test: Inside, outside, at boundaries

**Content Manipulation (3 methods)**:

9. **Range.deleteContents()** - Delete range contents
   - Spec: specs/dom.md lines 5400-5500
   - Complexity: HIGH (complex algorithm, partial node removal, mutation observers)
   - Test: Fully contained nodes, partially contained, collapsed range

10. **Range.extractContents()** - Extract to DocumentFragment
    - Spec: specs/dom.md lines 5510-5620
    - Complexity: HIGH (like delete but returns fragment, complex edge cases)
    - Test: Extract text, extract elements, partial extraction

11. **Range.cloneContents()** - Clone to DocumentFragment
    - Spec: specs/dom.md lines 5630-5720
    - Complexity: HIGH (uses cloneNode, preserves structure)
    - **Requires**: Node.cloneNode() from Phase 1 ✅
    - Test: Clone text, clone elements, partial cloning

**Insertion (2 methods)**:

12. **Range.insertNode(node)** - Insert node at range start
    - Spec: specs/dom.md lines 5730-5780
    - Complexity: MEDIUM (insertion with split, range update)
    - Test: Insert in text, insert at element boundary

13. **Range.surroundContents(newParent)** - Wrap range with element
    - Spec: specs/dom.md lines 5790-5850
    - Complexity: HIGH (validates partial containment, extracts and wraps)
    - Test: Valid wrapping, partial node error, text wrapping

**Additional (2 methods)**:

14. **Range.cloneRange()** - Clone the range object
    - Spec: specs/dom.md ~line 5860
    - Complexity: LOW (copy boundary points)
    - Test: Clone collapsed, clone normal range

15. **Range.intersectsNode(node)** - Check node intersection
    - Spec: specs/dom.md ~line 5930
    - Complexity: MEDIUM (position comparison)
    - Test: Fully contained, partially contained, outside

**Implementation Notes**:
- Range operations are CRITICAL for text editors and selection APIs
- deleteContents/extractContents/cloneContents have complex partial node handling
- Range boundaries are live - updates tracked by range_tracking.zig
- surroundContents validates that no partial nodes exist (except text)
- All content mutations must fire mutation observers

**Files to Modify**:
- webidl/src/dom/Range.zig - Add all method implementations
- src/dom/range_algorithms.zig - Create new file for complex algorithms
- tests/dom/range_boundaries_test.zig - Boundary manipulation tests
- tests/dom/range_content_test.zig - Content manipulation tests
- tests/dom/range_comparison_test.zig - Comparison tests

**Dependencies**:
- Phase 1: Node.cloneNode() - REQUIRED for cloneContents()
- src/dom/range_tracking.zig - Range updates (already exists)
- src/dom/tree.zig - Tree operations
- src/dom/mutation.zig - Mutation observers

**Success Criteria**:
✅ All 13+ algorithms implemented per spec (setStartBefore/After and setEndBefore/After count as 4)
✅ Complex algorithms (delete/extract/clone/surround) handle partial nodes correctly
✅ Range boundaries update correctly during mutations
✅ Mutation observers fire for all content changes
✅ All tests pass with zero memory leaks
✅ Edge cases handled (collapsed ranges, detached nodes, partial containment)

title: Fix TextDecoderStream to pass notPassed\(\) for transformer parameter
description:
## Summary

TextDecoderStream incorrectly passes a Zig stack pointer as the `transformer` argument to TransformStream. This causes a segfault when TransformStream tries to use it as a V8 Object handle.

## Current Broken Code

**File**: `src/webidl/impls/TextDecoderStream.zig:180-187`

```zig
var empty_transformer: u8 = 0\; // Placeholder for null transformer
const transform = try interfaces.TransformStream.call_constructor\(
    allocator,
    ctx,
    webidl.Opt\(*const anyopaque\).passed\(\&empty_transformer\),  // BUG\!
    webidl.Opt\(dictionaries.QueuingStrategy\).notPassed\(\),
    webidl.Opt\(dictionaries.QueuingStrategy\).notPassed\(\),
\)\;
```

### Problems

1. `empty_transformer` is a `u8` on the stack \(1-byte, arbitrary alignment\)
2. `\&empty_transformer` produces a pointer like `0x16f33296f` \(odd address\)
3. This pointer is passed as `*const anyopaque` to TransformStream
4. TransformStream casts it to `*v8.Object` and crashes

## Required Fix

**Option A \(Recommended\)**: Pass `notPassed\(\)` instead of a fake transformer:

```zig
const transform = try interfaces.TransformStream.call_constructor\(
    allocator,
    ctx,
    webidl.Opt\(*const anyopaque\).notPassed\(\),  // No transformer needed
    webidl.Opt\(dictionaries.QueuingStrategy\).notPassed\(\),
    webidl.Opt\(dictionaries.QueuingStrategy\).notPassed\(\),
\)\;
```

**Option B**: Use the internal algorithm setup directly:

Per the Encoding Standard, TextDecoderStream should set up its own internal transform/flush algorithms, not delegate to a JavaScript transformer. The current architecture passes a "placeholder" but should instead:

1. Create TransformStream with no transformer
2. Set up internal Zig-based transform/flush algorithms on the controller

## Spec Reference

**Encoding Standard §10.2.1**: "TextDecoderStream" 
- https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-textdecoderstream

The spec says TextDecoderStream should have internal transform and flush algorithms, not a JavaScript transformer object.

## Testing

After fix:
```bash
zig build wpt
# Should pass test 73 \(encoding/bom-handling.html\) without segfault
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] TextDecoderStream does NOT pass a stack pointer to TransformStream
- [ ] Uses `webidl.Opt\(*const anyopaque\).notPassed\(\)` OR proper internal setup
- [ ] Test 73 \(`encoding/bom-handling.html`\) runs without segfault
- [ ] TextDecoderStream still functions correctly \(decode operations work\)

title: Epic: CSP Module Implementation
description:
Implement the Content Security Policy (CSP) Level 3 module required for Trusted Types enforcement.

## Overview
CSP is a critical dependency for Trusted Types - the trusted-types and require-trusted-types-for directives control policy creation and sink enforcement. This epic covers implementing a complete CSP parsing, enforcement, and violation reporting system.

## Spec Reference  
- CSP Level 3: https://www.w3.org/TR/CSP3/
- Local spec: specs/w3c/csp.md

## Core Concepts

1. **Policy** - Contains directive set, disposition (enforce/report), source (header/meta)
2. **Directive** - Name/value pair controlling specific behavior
3. **Source Expression** - Allowlist entries ('self', hosts, schemes, nonces, hashes)
4. **CSP List** - Multiple policies applied to a document/worker
5. **Violation** - Security violation object for reporting

## Key Directives for Trusted Types

- `trusted-types <policy-names>` - Controls which policy names can be created
- `require-trusted-types-for 'script'` - Enables enforcement for DOM XSS sinks
- `script-src` with `'trusted-types-eval'` - Delegates eval() to Trusted Types

## Sub-tasks
1. CSP core data structures (Policy, Directive, SourceList)
2. CSP parsing algorithms
3. Source expression matching
4. Directive fallback chains
5. Trusted Types directives
6. Violation reporting infrastructure
7. Integration hooks (Fetch, DOM, HTML)
8. Comprehensive tests

## Deliverables
- src/csp/ module
- tests/csp/

## Estimated Effort: 7-10 days

description:
CRITICAL memory safety - base field cleanup missing in deinit().

**Root Cause:** WebIDL codegen has injectBaseFieldInit() that auto-adds base field initialization to init() methods, but NO equivalent injectBaseFieldDeinit() for deinit() methods.

**Impact:** Memory leaks in event_listener_list (from EventTarget), child_nodes and registered_observers (from Node) for all classes with inheritance.

**Proper Fix:** Add injectBaseFieldDeinit() function to src/webidl/codegen/codegen.zig that:
1. Mirrors injectBaseFieldInit() pattern
2. Walks inheritance chain to find fields needing cleanup
3. Injects cleanup code before closing brace of deinit()
4. Auto-fixes all 8+ affected classes

**Implementation:** See tmp/codegen_deinit_fix_analysis.md for complete specification with code examples.

**Estimate:** 4-5 hours (2-3 impl + 1-2 test)

**Alternative (not recommended):** Manual cleanup in 8 source files - doesn't scale, inconsistent with init() pattern.

title: 7.5: SharedWorker MessagePort connections
description:
# 7.5: SharedWorker MessagePort connections

## Objective
Implement proper MessagePort pair creation for SharedWorker connections.

## Current State
- SharedWorker and SharedWorkerManager exist
- connect() has TODO: "Create MessagePort pair"
- onconnect event not fired

## Implementation

1. On new SharedWorker(): create MessagePort pair
2. Return one port to caller (sharedWorker.port)
3. Queue connect event to worker with other port
4. Fire connect event with ports property containing the port

## Connect Event Flow
new SharedWorker(url):
  -> Find or create SharedWorker
  -> Create MessagePort pair (port1, port2)
  -> Set sharedWorker.port = port1
  -> Queue MessageEvent to worker with port2 in ports
  -> Worker's onconnect receives event
  -> Worker uses event.ports[0] to communicate

## Files to Modify
- src/html/workers/shared_worker.zig - Port pair creation
- src/html/workers/shared_worker_manager.zig - Connect handling
- src/webidl/impls/SharedWorkerGlobalScope.zig - onconnect dispatch

## Tests
- new SharedWorker().port is a MessagePort
- Worker onconnect receives event with port
- Multiple connections get separate ports
- Communication works both directions

## Estimated Size
- 250-400 lines

## Depends On

description:
## Summary

Replace direct string input in Tokenizer/TreeBuilder with InputStreamManager to support dynamic content insertion via document.write\(\).

## Current State

- Tokenizer is initialized with a static string: `Tokenizer.init\(allocator, html\)`
- InputStreamManager exists in `document_write.zig` with support for insertions
- But Tokenizer doesn't use InputStreamManager

## Required Changes

1. **Modify Tokenizer** to use InputStreamManager:
   ```zig
   pub fn initWithStream\(allocator: Allocator, stream: *InputStreamManager\) Tokenizer {
       return .{
           .allocator = allocator,
           .input_stream = stream,
           // ...
       }\;
   }
   ```

2. **Update character reading** to go through InputStreamManager:
   ```zig
   fn nextInputChar\(self: *Tokenizer\) ?u21 {
       return self.input_stream.getNextChar\(\)\;
   }
   ```

3. **Pass InputStreamManager to TreeBuilder**:
   - TreeBuilder needs access to insert content during script execution
   - When script calls document.write\(\), content goes to stream

4. **Wire up document.write\(\)** in script execution:
   - Get InputStreamManager from parser context
   - Call `stream.insert\(content\)` at insertion point

## Integration Flow

```
script.document.write\("content"\)
       ↓
DocumentWriteState.documentWrite\(\)
       ↓
InputStreamManager.insert\(\)
       ↓
Tokenizer sees inserted content
       ↓
New tokens processed by TreeBuilder
```

## Files to Modify

- `src/html/parser/tokenizer.zig` \(use InputStreamManager\)
- `src/html/parser/tree_builder.zig` \(pass stream reference\)
- `src/html/document_write.zig` \(integration with parser\)
- `src/webidl/impls/Document.zig` \(document.write impl\)

## Test Criteria

```html
\<script\>
  document.write\('\<div id="written"\>Hello\</div\>'\)\;
\</script\>
\<script\>
  console.log\(document.getElementById\('written'\).textContent\)\; // "Hello"
\</script\>
```

IMPLEMENTATION:

- Full CSS Selectors Level 4 tokenizer
- Complete recursive descent parser with specificity
- All structural pseudo-classes (:first-child, :nth-child, etc.)
- All logical pseudo-classes (:not, :is, :where, :has)

Implement the top-level fetch() entry point that ties all algorithms together.

**Spec Reference:** https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#fetch-method

**Algorithm Steps:**
1. Let p be a new promise
2. Let requestObject be the input Request
3. Let request be requestObject's internal request
4. Let globalObject be relevant global object
5. If request's signal is aborted, reject p with AbortError
6. Let responseObject be a new Response
7. Run main fetch with request
8. On response, resolve p with responseObject

**Key Dependencies:**
- Main fetch (Phase 6.2)
- Request WebIDL interface (Phase 7.2)
- Response WebIDL interface (Phase 7.3)
- AbortSignal (already implemented)

**Files:**
- src/fetch/fetch.zig (top-level entry point)
- src/fetch/algorithms/fetch_entry.zig

**Estimated Time:** 2-3 days

title: Add pointer untagging to binding.zig V8 FFI functions
description:
## Overview

The V8 binding layer in `src/runtime/engines/v8/binding.zig` has multiple functions that receive tagged pointers but pass them directly to V8 FFI without untagging.

## Affected Functions \(from analysis\)

### Line ~467 - v8FromJSValue
Converts JS values - must untag before FFI calls.

### Line ~509 - v8IsInstanceOf
Instance type checking - receives tagged pointers from conversion layer.

### Line ~528 - v8UnwrapInstance
Unwraps Zig instances from V8 objects - must handle tagged pointers.

### Lines ~656, ~691 - Value access functions
Any function that accesses V8 values via FFI.

## Required Changes

### 1. Import pointer_tag module
```zig
const pointer_tag = @import\("pointer_tag.zig"\)\;
```

### 2. Add untagging to each affected function

Pattern to apply:
```zig
// BEFORE \(wrong\)
fn someFunction\(js_value: *const anyopaque\) ReturnType {
    const value: *ffi.Value = @ptrCast\(@alignCast\(@constCast\(js_value\)\)\)\;
    return ffi.v8_SomeFunction\(value\)\;
}

// AFTER \(correct\)
fn someFunction\(js_value: *const anyopaque\) ReturnType {
    const untagged = pointer_tag.untagPointer\(js_value\)\;
    const value: *ffi.Value = @ptrCast\(untagged.ptr\)\;
    return ffi.v8_SomeFunction\(value\)\;
}
```

## Full Audit Required

Search binding.zig for:
1. All functions with `anyopaque` parameters
2. All `@ptrCast` operations on external pointers
3. All V8 FFI calls with pointer arguments

## File-Specific Patterns

The binding.zig file handles:
- Property access \(get/set\)
- Method calls
- Instance wrapping/unwrapping
- Type checking \(isObject, isFunction, etc.\)
- Object creation

Each category may have tagged pointer issues.

title: V8 callback persistence: Local handles become invalid after constructor returns
description:
## Problem

When V8 callbacks (like , , ,  in WritableStream) are stored for later invocation, they become invalid because they are stored as raw pointers to Local handles instead of Global handles.

## Root Cause

In  lines 941-951:


The  parameter is a Local V8 handle that becomes invalid when the JavaScript call stack returns. When we try to invoke the callback later (e.g., in ), the pointer is garbage.

## Symptoms

-  crashes with "misaligned address" error
- The crash occurs when trying to invoke the stored callback
- Only affects streams with callbacks - empty streams work fine

## Affected Code

- 
- Any code that stores V8 callbacks from dictionaries for later use
- WritableStreamDefaultController internal state stores these invalid pointers

## Solution

Callbacks that need to persist beyond the current call stack must be stored as Global handles:

1. When converting  for callback storage, create a Global handle
2. Store the Global handle pointer instead of the Local handle pointer
3. When invoking the callback, use the Global handle to get a Local
4. Free the Global handle when the callback is no longer needed

## Related

- This is similar to how  manages Global handles for wrapper identity
- The  and related functions can be used

Fix misaligned address crash in WritableStream.invokePendingStartCallback
description:
## Problem

When running WPT test `encoding/streams/decode-bad-chunks.any.js`, a crash occurs:

```
thread panic: load of misaligned address 0x6b204ef24ed for type 'const Address'
src/webidl/impls/WritableStream.zig:953:32: in invokePendingStartCallback
    if \(\!v8.v8_Value_IsFunction\(v8_value\)\) {
```

## Root Cause

In `invokePendingStartCallback\(\)`, the `start_algorithm` pointer \(stored as `*const anyopaque`\) is being directly cast to `*v8.Value`:

```zig
const v8_value: *v8.Value = @ptrCast\(@alignCast\(@constCast\(start_algo\)\)\)\;
```

The stored pointer may not actually be a valid V8 Value pointer, causing a misaligned address when V8 tries to read from it.

## Related

This is similar to the issue fixed in `call_pipeThrough` \(whatwg-n3tpw\) where `*const anyopaque` was incorrectly assumed to be a valid V8 pointer.

## Location

- File: `src/webidl/impls/WritableStream.zig:951-953`
- Function: `invokePendingStartCallback`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] WPT test `decode-bad-chunks.any.js` runs without crashing
- [ ] Start callbacks are properly validated before use

Fix CallbackWrapper to use V8 persistent handles \(ROOT CAUSE\)
description:
## Summary

`CallbackWrapper` in `src/runtime/engines/v8/callback_wrapper.zig` stores raw V8 `Local\<Function\>` and `Local\<Object\>` pointers without creating persistent handles. This is the ROOT CAUSE of callback lifetime issues throughout the codebase.

## Current Broken Code

```zig
pub const CallbackWrapper = struct {
    callback_function: ?*v8.Function,   // Line 41 - RAW LOCAL POINTER
    callback_object: ?*v8.Object,       // Line 44 - RAW LOCAL POINTER
    // ...
}\;
```

## Critical TODOs Already in Code

- Line 94-95: "TODO: Dispose persistent handles when FFI supports v8_Function_Dispose/v8_Object_Dispose"
- Line 198-199: "TODO: Use persistent handles when FFI supports v8_Function_Persist"
- Line 218-219: "TODO: Use persistent handles when FFI supports v8_Object_Persist"

## Impact

This affects EVERYTHING that stores callbacks:
- EventTarget.addEventListener
- WebSocket.onopen/onerror/onclose/onmessage
- XMLHttpRequest.onreadystatechange
- MutationObserver
- All event handlers

## Required Changes

1. Change `callback_function` to use `GlobalHandle` or `*ffi.Value` \(Global\)
2. Change `callback_object` to use `GlobalHandle` or `*ffi.Value` \(Global\)
3. Create Global handles in constructor/setters
4. Dispose Global handles in destructor
5. Use `v8_Global_Get` to retrieve Local handles for invocation

## FFI Functions Available

- `v8_Value_ToGlobal\(isolate, local\)` - Create Global from Local
- `v8_Global_Dispose\(global\)` - Dispose Global handle
- `v8_Global_Get\(isolate, global\)` - Get Local from Global
- `v8_Global_ToFunction\(global\)` - Cast Global to Function

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] CallbackWrapper stores Global handles, not Local handles
- [ ] Global handles created when callback is set
- [ ] Global handles disposed in deinit/destroy
- [ ] All callback invocations work correctly
- [ ] No memory leaks

Implement FileReader read-operation algorithm and state machine
description:
## Summary
Implement the FileReader `read operation` algorithm and state machine in `src/file/algorithms/read_operation.zig` and `src/file/file_reader_internals.zig`.

## Spec Reference
- W3C File API §6.2: The FileReader API
- W3C File API §6.2.3: Reading a File or Blob
- https://www.w3.org/TR/FileAPI/#reading-a-file

## FileReader States
```zig
pub const FileReaderState = enum(u16) {
    EMPTY = 0,    // No read initiated
    LOADING = 1,  // Read in progress
    DONE = 2,     // Read complete (success, error, or abort)
};
```

## Read Operation Algorithm (from spec)

A FileReader `fr` has an associated **read operation** algorithm, given `blob`, a `type`, and an optional `encodingName`:

1. If fr's state is "loading", throw an InvalidStateError DOMException.
2. Set fr's state to "loading".
3. Set fr's result to null.
4. Set fr's error to null.
5. Let stream be the result of calling get stream on blob.
6. Let reader be the result of getting a reader from stream.
7. Let bytes be an empty byte sequence.
8. Let chunkPromise be the result of reading a chunk from stream with reader.
9. Let isFirstChunk be true.
10. In parallel, while true:
    a. Wait for chunkPromise to be fulfilled or rejected.
    b. If chunkPromise is fulfilled, and isFirstChunk is true, queue a task to fire a progress event called "loadstart" at fr.
    c. Set isFirstChunk to false.
    d. If chunkPromise is fulfilled with an object whose done property is false:
       i. Append the bytes to bytes.
       ii. If roughly 50ms have passed since last progress, queue a task to fire a progress event called "progress" at fr.
       iii. Set chunkPromise to the result of reading a chunk.
    e. If chunkPromise is fulfilled with done property true:
       i. Set fr's state to "done".
       ii. Let result be the result of package data given bytes, type, blob's type, and encodingName.
       iii. If package data threw, set fr's error and fire "error" event.
       iv. Else set fr's result and fire "load" event.
       v. If fr's state is not "loading", fire "loadend" event.
    f. If chunkPromise is rejected:
       i. Set fr's state to "done".
       ii. Set fr's error to the rejection reason.
       iii. Fire "error" event.
       iv. If fr's state is not "loading", fire "loadend" event.

## Implementation

### FileReaderData (`src/file/file_reader_internals.zig`)
```zig
pub const FileReaderData = struct {
    state: FileReaderState = .EMPTY,
    result: ?ResultUnion = null,
    error_value: ?*runtime.DOMException = null,
    
    // Progress tracking
    bytes_loaded: u64 = 0,
    last_progress_time: i64 = 0,
    
    // Event handlers
    onloadstart: ?typedefs.EventHandler = null,
    onprogress: ?typedefs.EventHandler = null,
    onload: ?typedefs.EventHandler = null,
    onabort: ?typedefs.EventHandler = null,
    onerror: ?typedefs.EventHandler = null,
    onloadend: ?typedefs.EventHandler = null,
    
    allocator: std.mem.Allocator,
};

pub const ResultUnion = union(enum) {
    string: []const u8,      // For readAsText, readAsDataURL, readAsBinaryString
    array_buffer: *runtime.ArrayBuffer, // For readAsArrayBuffer
};
```

### Read Operation (`src/file/algorithms/read_operation.zig`)
```zig
pub fn readOperation(
    allocator: std.mem.Allocator,
    file_reader: *FileReaderData,
    blob_data: *const BlobData,
    read_type: ReadType,
    encoding_name: ?[]const u8,
    event_loop: *EventLoop,
) !void {
    // Step 1: Check state
    if (file_reader.state == .LOADING) {
        return error.InvalidStateError;
    }
    
    // Steps 2-4: Initialize state
    file_reader.state = .LOADING;
    file_reader.result = null;
    file_reader.error_value = null;
    
    // Steps 5-6: Get stream and reader
    const stream = try createBlobStream(allocator, blob_data);
    const reader = try stream.getReader(.{});
    
    // Steps 7-10: Async read loop
    event_loop.queueTask(.{
        .callback = readChunkCallback,
        .context = &ReadContext{
            .file_reader = file_reader,
            .reader = reader,
            .bytes = std.ArrayList(u8).init(allocator),
            .read_type = read_type,
            .encoding_name = encoding_name,
            .is_first_chunk = true,
            .blob_type = blob_data.getType(),
        },
    });
}
```

## Progress Events
- Fire `loadstart` after first chunk received
- Fire `progress` every ~50ms during read
- Fire `load` on successful completion
- Fire `error` on failure
- Fire `abort` when abort() called
- Fire `loadend` at end (always, unless new read started)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] State machine (EMPTY -> LOADING -> DONE)
- [ ] Throws InvalidStateError if already LOADING
- [ ] Reads blob via stream
- [ ] Fires loadstart after first chunk
- [ ] Fires progress every ~50ms
- [ ] Packages data according to read type
- [ ] Sets result on success
- [ ] Sets error on failure
- [ ] Fires appropriate end events
- [ ] Handles abort correctly
- [ ] Integration with event loop
- [ ] All tests pass

description:
## Summary

CompressionStream and DecompressionStream may have the same bug as TextDecoderStream - passing an invalid Zig pointer as the transformer argument to TransformStream.

## Files to Audit

- `src/webidl/impls/CompressionStream.zig`
- `src/webidl/impls/DecompressionStream.zig`

## What to Look For

1. Search for `TransformStream.call_constructor` calls
2. Check what is passed as the `transformer` argument
3. Look for patterns like:
   - `var empty_transformer: u8 = 0\; ... \&empty_transformer`
   - Any stack-allocated variable being passed as `*const anyopaque`
   - Arbitrary values being wrapped in `webidl.Opt\(*const anyopaque\).passed\(\)`

```zig
// BAD - passing Zig stack pointer
var placeholder: u8 = 0\;
webidl.Opt\(*const anyopaque\).passed\(\&placeholder\)
```

## Correct Pattern

```zig
// GOOD - explicitly indicate no transformer
webidl.Opt\(*const anyopaque\).notPassed\(\)
```

If either stream has the same bug, apply the same fix:
1. Change `.passed\(\&something\)` to `.notPassed\(\)`

## Spec Reference

- https://wicg.github.io/compression/

CompressionStream and DecompressionStream should have internal transform/flush algorithms for compression/decompression, not JavaScript transformers.

title: Audit interface.zig for tagged pointer handling in constructor callbacks
description:
## Overview

The `src/runtime/engines/v8/interface.zig` file handles constructor callbacks and argument extraction. While the crash originates downstream in engine.zig, there may be additional tagged pointer issues in interface.zig.

## Key Code Paths to Audit

### constructorCallback \(Line ~1473-1579\)
Entry point for all WebIDL interface constructors. Extracts arguments from V8 and calls the Zig constructor.

### callConstructorWithArgs \(Line ~1585-1798\)
Dispatches to the correct constructor based on argument count. Uses `conv.fromV8Value` which produces tagged pointers.

### getInstance \(Line ~3073-3075\)
```zig
pub fn getInstance\(comptime T: type, object: *v8.Object\) ?*T {
    const ptr = v8.v8_Object_GetAlignedPointerFromInternalField\(object, 0\)\;
    if \(ptr == null\) return null\;
    return @ptrCast\(@alignCast\(ptr\)\)\;
}
```
This receives a V8 Object - verify the object pointer itself isn't tagged.

### Method/Property callbacks
All callbacks that receive arguments from JavaScript may encounter tagged pointers.

## Analysis Questions

1. **Are constructor arguments tagged?**
   - `fromV8Value` returns tagged pointers for `*const anyopaque`
   - These are passed to interface constructors
   - Constructors must handle tagged pointers OR untagging must happen earlier

2. **Are callback object parameters tagged?**
   - When V8 invokes callbacks, does it pass tagged pointers?
   - The FunctionCallbackInfo object provides V8 handles

3. **Are internal field pointers tagged?**
   - `v8_Object_GetAlignedPointerFromInternalField` returns raw pointers
   - These should NOT be tagged \(they're Zig allocations\)
   - But verify this assumption

## Required Actions

### 1. Trace all pointer flows
Document each function that receives/passes pointers:
- Input source \(V8 callback, conversion, internal field\)
- Whether tagging is applied
- Where untagging should occur

### 2. Identify untagging boundaries
Determine the correct layer for untagging:
- Should `fromV8Value` NOT tag certain types?
- Should engine/binding functions always untag?
- Should interface.zig untag before calling impls?

### 3. Add defensive checks
```zig
// Optional: Add debug assertion
if \(builtin.mode == .Debug\) {
    const tag = pointer_tag.getTag\(ptr\)\;
    if \(tag \!= .untagged\) {
        @panic\("Tagged pointer passed to FFI boundary"\)\;
    }
}
```

## Testing

1. Add logging to trace pointer values through constructor flow
2. Verify pointer alignment at each stage
3. Test constructors with various argument types

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All pointer flows documented
- [ ] No tagged pointers reach V8 FFI
- [ ] Constructor callbacks work correctly
- [ ] Method callbacks work correctly
- [ ] Build succeeds

Epic: Fix V8 Handle Lifetime in conversions.zig \(Option A - Production Fix\)
description:
# Epic: Fix V8 Handle Lifetime in conversions.zig \(Option A - Production Fix\)

## Problem Statement

When V8 converts JavaScript objects to Zig dictionaries, callback functions \(stored as `*const anyopaque`\) are returned as raw `Local\<Value\>` pointers. These Local handles become **dangling pointers** after the HandleScope ends. When we later try to use them \(e.g., create a Global handle, invoke the callback\), they're already invalid → **SEGFAULT**.

### Crash Signature
```
Segmentation fault at address 0x8
v8_Value_ToGlobal \(v8_wrapper.cpp\)
  → global_handles.zig:68 in create
  → algorithm.zig:151 in jsCallbackAlgorithmGlobal
  → ReadableStream.zig:2063 in setUpReadableStreamDefaultController
```

### Root Cause Location
`src/runtime/engines/v8/conversions.zig` \(lines ~928-938\):
```zig
if \(T == *const anyopaque\) {
    // Returns raw Local pointer - becomes dangling after scope ends\!
    return @ptrCast\(value\)\;
}
```

## Why Option A \(Fix in conversions.zig\) is Best

### 1. Single Point of Fix
- Fixes the problem once, at the source
- All dictionary extractions automatically benefit
- No need to remember to handle this in every stream/callback implementation

### 2. Correct Architectural Boundary
- The conversion layer is responsible for translating V8 → Zig
- It should produce values that are safe to use after the conversion
- Currently it's leaking V8 implementation details \(Local handle lifetime\) to callers

### 3. Prevents Future Bugs
- Any new code using `*const anyopaque` for callbacks will automatically work
- Developers don't need to know about V8 handle lifetimes
- Less surface area for mistakes

### 4. Matches V8 Best Practices
- V8's own documentation says: "Use Global handles for values that need to persist beyond a HandleScope"
- The conversion layer crossing a scope boundary is exactly when this matters

## Implementation Approach

### Core Change in conversions.zig
```zig
if \(T == *const anyopaque\) {
    // Check if this is a function/object that needs to persist beyond HandleScope
    if \(ffi.v8_Value_IsFunction\(value\) or ffi.v8_Value_IsObject\(value\)\) {
        // Create a Global handle so it survives after this scope
        if \(ffi.v8_Value_ToGlobal\(isolate, value\)\) \|global\| {
            return @ptrCast\(global\)\;
        }
    }
    // For primitives \(numbers, strings, booleans\), the value is copied
    // so we can return the Local pointer \(or better: extract the primitive\)
    return @ptrCast\(value\)\;
}
```

### Memory Management Strategy: Weak Handles

The key challenge is: **who disposes the Global handles?**

**Solution: Use V8 Weak Handles with GC callbacks**
- V8 will automatically clean up when JavaScript no longer references them
- This matches JavaScript semantics perfectly
- No manual disposal tracking needed
- More correct than manual disposal

```cpp
// Create a weak Global that V8 can GC when JS drops all references
extern "C" Global\<Value\>* v8_Value_ToWeakGlobal\(
    Isolate* isolate, 
    Local\<Value\> local,
    void* weak_callback_data,
    weak_callback_fn callback
\)\;
```

## Trade-offs Analysis

\| Aspect \| Option A \(conversions.zig\) \| Option B \(each impl\) \|
\|--------\|---------------------------\|---------------------\|
\| Code changes \| 1 place \| 3+ stream impls \|
\| Future-proof \| ✅ Yes \| ❌ Must remember \|
\| Memory management \| Automatic via weak handles \| Manual in each impl \|
\| Performance \| Slightly more Globals \| Minimal \|
\| Complexity \| Low \(centralized\) \| High \(scattered\) \|

## Success Criteria

1. ✅ Dictionary conversion creates Global handles for functions/objects
2. ✅ Callbacks survive beyond initial HandleScope
3. ✅ Weak handles allow V8 GC to clean up unused callbacks
4. ✅ No memory leaks \(verify with ASAN/Valgrind\)
5. ✅ WPT test `encoding/streams/decode-bad-chunks.any.js` passes \(no crash\)
6. ✅ All existing stream tests continue to pass
7. ✅ No regressions in other dictionary conversions

## Dependencies

- whatwg-e702t: V8 Global handle FFI functions \(foundation\)

## Files to Modify

1. **Primary**: `src/runtime/engines/v8/conversions.zig`
2. **FFI**: `src/runtime/engines/v8/v8_wrapper.cpp` \(weak handle support\)
3. **FFI**: `src/runtime/engines/v8/ffi.zig` \(weak handle declarations\)
4. **Helper**: `src/runtime/engines/v8/global_handles.zig` \(weak handle wrapper\)

## Related Issues \(to close after this epic\)

- whatwg-n5a3c: Add V8 object unwrapping \(superseded by this fix\)
- whatwg-ewih6: Fix call_pipeThrough \(symptom, not root cause\)

## Estimated Effort

- Phase 1 \(FFI\): 1 day
- Phase 2 \(conversions.zig\): 1 day  
- Phase 3 \(weak handles\): 1-2 days
- Phase 4 \(testing\): 1 day
- **Total: 4-5 days**

title: Add defensive null checks in streams internal state access
description:
## Overview

Multiple places in the streams implementation access `state.own._internal` without proper null checking, which can lead to segfaults if the internal state is not properly initialized. While the root cause should be fixed \(V8 pointer type mismatch\), defensive programming requires proper null checks at all access points.

## Current State

The streams implementation uses a pattern where:
1. `State.own._internal` is an optional pointer: `?*InternalState`
2. Most code uses `orelse return error.InvalidState` pattern
3. Some code paths may have missing checks

## Audit Required

Review all accesses to `_internal` in these files:

### ReadableStream
- `src/webidl/impls/ReadableStream.zig`
- Look for: `state.own._internal` access patterns
- Verify all have null checks

### WritableStream  
- `src/webidl/impls/WritableStream.zig`
- `WritableStreamImpl.InternalState` accesses
- Verify initialization paths

### TransformStream
- `src/webidl/impls/TransformStream.zig`
- `internal.readableStream` and `internal.writableStream` accesses

### Controllers
- `src/webidl/impls/ReadableStreamDefaultController.zig`
- `src/webidl/impls/WritableStreamDefaultController.zig`
- `src/webidl/impls/TransformStreamDefaultController.zig`
- `src/webidl/impls/ReadableByteStreamController.zig`

### Readers/Writers
- `src/webidl/impls/ReadableStreamDefaultReader.zig`
- `src/webidl/impls/ReadableStreamBYOBReader.zig`
- `src/webidl/impls/WritableStreamDefaultWriter.zig`

## Pattern to Verify

Each access should follow this pattern:
```zig
// GOOD: Proper null check
const internal = state.own._internal orelse return error.InvalidState\;

// BAD: No null check \(could crash\)
const internal = state.own._internal.?\;  // Crashes if null

// BAD: Assumes non-null without check
const internal = state.own._internal\;
internal.some_field\;  // Crashes if null
```

## Implementation

1. **Audit all files** listed above for `_internal` access
2. **Add missing null checks** where found
3. **Return appropriate errors**:
   - `error.InvalidState` for uninitialized streams
   - `error.TypeError` if spec requires TypeError

## Edge Cases to Consider

1. **Double-initialization**: What if `_internal` is set twice?
2. **Use-after-deinit**: What if stream is deinitialized but reference held?
3. **Partial initialization**: What if constructor fails mid-way?
4. **TransformStream children**: ReadableStream and WritableStream created by TransformStream must have `_internal` set

## Testing

Add tests for:
```zig
test "ReadableStream methods return InvalidState if not initialized" {
    // Create instance via init\(\) not call_constructor\(\)
    const instance = try interfaces.ReadableStream.init\(allocator, ctx\)\;
    defer instance.deinit\(\)\;
    
    // Verify methods return error, not crash
    try testing.expectError\(error.InvalidState, instance.getReader\(\)\)\;
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All `_internal` accesses audited in streams impls
- [ ] Missing null checks added
- [ ] Tests added for uninitialized state access
- [ ] No crashes when accessing methods on uninitialized streams
- [ ] Proper error messages returned

## Parent Epic

# 7.2: Worker isolation with separate V8 contexts

## Objective
Run workers in isolated V8 contexts (same thread initially, true isolates later).

## Current State
- Workers run in same context as main thread
- No isolation between worker and main thread
- WorkerGlobalScope not properly set up

## Implementation Approach
Start with same-thread isolation (simpler), upgrade to true threads later:

### Phase A: Same-thread isolation
1. Create new V8 Context for each worker
2. Set up WorkerGlobalScope as global object
3. Run worker event loop interleaved with main
4. Use structured clone for message passing (already implemented)

### Phase B: True threading (future)
1. Create new V8 Isolate per worker
2. Run on separate OS thread
3. Use thread-safe message queue

## Files to Modify
- src/html/workers/worker_agent.zig - Context creation
- src/html/workers/dedicated_worker.zig - Isolate setup
- src/runtime/engines/v8/ - Worker context initialization
- src/webidl/impls/WorkerGlobalScope.zig - Global setup

## Tests
- Worker has separate global scope
- Variables in worker don't leak to main
- Worker can't access main thread DOM
- Multiple workers have separate contexts

## Estimated Size
- 500-800 lines

The V8 snapshot generator fails with "CheckGlobalAndEternalHandles failed" because Global handles are stored in Zig/C++ static memory during interface registration. These handles are not part of the serialized context and cause V8 to fail during .

## Solution: Don't Cache Templates in Snapshot Mode

The cleanest solution is to NOT store Global handles in Zig at all during snapshot creation:

1. Add a  parameter to registration functions
2. When :
   - Don't store templates in  (per-interface static)
   - Don't register in  (global registry)
   - Create templates as Local handles within HandleScope
   - Let V8 serialize only the attached constructors on the global object
3. At load time, templates are recreated from the snapshot context

## Why This Works

- V8 snapshots serialize the JavaScript heap, including constructor functions attached to 
- The template caches are Zig-side caching - not needed for snapshot creation
- By only creating Local handles (not Global), V8 has nothing to complain about
- At load time, V8 recreates the heap from the snapshot

## Key Files

-  - The snapshot generator tool
-  - V8Interface with  and 
-  - Global template registry
-  - C++ wrapper with static handles
-  - FFI declarations

## Success Criteria

1. Snapshot creation completes without errors
2. Snapshot loading works and interfaces are available
3. Normal (non-snapshot) mode still uses caching for performance
4. WPT tests pass with snapshot-loaded contexts
